label: Add to Album
params_doc: {id: albumId, ids?: [photoIds]} (default: selection) → {added, skipped}; Local photos are skipped (albums hold library photos), only Local ones is an error; ids the library doesn't have are dropped; nothing new to add changes nothing (no undo step)

params_doc: {name, rules?: partial Filter (rating, ratingOp, flag, flags, label, labels, kind, edited, keyword, camera, lens, dateFrom, dateTo, date, text, album, ruleSet: {match: all|any|none, rules: [{field, op, value} | {group: ruleSet}]} — see album.ruleFields), parent?: folderId} — without `rules`, saves the current view (source + filter)

params_doc: {id} — deletes the album or folder and its descendants, keeping photos in the library; one undo step

label: Move Album
params_doc: {id, parent?: folderId|null}

params_doc: {id?: albumId (default: the album on screen), ids?} — takes the photos out of the album only: they stay in the library and in their folders (issue #1805; photo.delete removes them from the library) → {removed, album: name}

params_doc: {id, name}

label: Reorder Album
params_doc: {id, parent?: folderId|null, before?: albumId|null} — places the album (or folder) in `parent` (default: where it is; null: the top level) before the sibling `before` of the same kind, or last of its kind; the folder is then ordered by hand. label: Smart Album Rule Fields
params_doc: {} → [{field, label, kind (text|keywords|number|date|choice|bool|album: an album id), group (field-menu submenu, null at the top level), ops: [{op, label}], choices? (ids), choiceLabels? ({id: label})}] for ruleSet rules, in menu order

params_doc: {id: albumId, photo?: photoId}

params_doc: {id, rules?: partial Filter merged onto the current rules (null clears a field), replace?: bool, fromView?: bool (use the current view), name?: also rename it (blank keeps the name) — one undo step, both or neither}

label: Set as Target Album
params_doc: {id: albumId | null} (null = the Quick Collection)

label: Sort Albums by Name
params_doc: {parent?: folderId|null} — drops the hand order of the albums inside the folder (default: the top level), so they are listed by name → {changed}: how many albums lost their place

params_doc: {ids?} — B: adds the photos to the target album (the Quick Collection unless one is set), or removes them when they're all in it → {album, added, toggled, skipped}; Local photos are skipped, ids the library doesn't have are dropped (none left: nothing changes and `added` is null)

label: GPU Rendering
params_doc: {enabled?: bool, wait?: bool} — allow/forbid GPU rendering (CPU fallback; LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0 forbids it for the process); returns {enabled, available, adapter, reason (why the GPU is off), lastFallback (latest render redone on the CPU, and why)}. wait: false never waits for a device still being created (available, adapter and reason are then null and the device is created in the background; with GPU rendering off they say so at once)

label: Hot Pixel Limit
params_doc: {percent?: number} — Remove Hot Pixels leaves a raw alone when more than this share of its photosites would be replaced (0.001..100 %, default 0.2 %; real light it keeps doesn't count); returns {percent, default}

label: Memory Budget
params_doc: {mb?: number} — set the memory budget shared by the caches (default: a quarter of RAM, at most 1536 MB); returns the report

label: Set Before
params_doc: {source: import|current|history|version, index? (history step), name? (version)} — what the before side shows (this session)

label: Query Photos
params_doc: {filter?: Filter, sort?: Sort, offset?, limit?} — omit filter to list the current view

params_doc: {aspect: "original"|"free"|"current" (lock the crop's present shape)|"toggle" (lock ↔ free)|"1x1"|"4x5"|"8.5x11"|"5x7"|"2x3"|"4x3"|"16x9"|"16x10"|[w,h], orientation?: "crop"|"given"} — a named ratio takes the crop's present orientation (landscape, or portrait after X); [w,h] is used as given (taller than wide → portrait); `orientation` overrides either

label: Auto Straighten
params_doc: {} — level the horizon (or plumb lines) with the crop angle

label: Drag Crop Handle
params_doc: {handle: topLeft|topRight|bottomRight|bottomLeft|top|right|bottom|left|move | 0..8, from: [x,y], to: [x,y] (normalized, straightened frame), start?: [x0,y0,x1,y1] (default: the current crop), keepRatio?: bool (default false)} — drags a crop handle; stops at the image edge, keeps the opposite edges, honours the aspect lock; keepRatio holds the frame's current proportions for this drag even with the lock off (the UI sends it while Shift is held)

params_doc: {rect?: [x0,y0,x1,y1] normalized in the straightened frame, angle?: degrees}

params_doc: {path, names?: [name] (default: every user preset)} — writes a .lccurve JSON file → {path, count}

params_doc: {path | paths: [file]} — .lccurve JSON files ({format, version, presets: [...]}, an array of presets, or one preset); same-named user presets are replaced → {imported: [name], failed: [[file, error]]}

label: Point Curve Presets
params_doc: {} → {presets: [{name, master, red, green, blue: [[x,y],...], builtin?}], current: name of the preset the active photo's point curves match, or null}

params_doc: {channel?: all|point|parametric|master|red|green|blue (default all)} — the active photo's tone curve (or one channel) back to linear

params_doc: {name} — the active photo's point curves under a name (replaces a user preset of that name; built-in names are reserved), saved with the library

params_doc: {id?, all?} → {cancelled} — stop the photo being made and/or forget the ones waiting (all of them when `id` is omitted)

label: Clear Denoise Cache
params_doc: {} → {deleted, bytes} — delete every cached denoised picture of this library (they are made again when wanted)

label: Download Denoise Model
params_doc: {id, acknowledged: true} → {started, from} — fetch a model LightCraft has a pinned address for (see `downloadHost` in the list) in the background over HTTPS with lightcraft-fetch. `acknowledged` must be true: the user has been shown the model's terms and accepted them. It is checked against its size and SHA-256, installed and chosen by itself; `denoise.models.downloads` shows how far it is

label: Cancel Denoise Model Download
params_doc: {id} → {discarded} — stop a download, or delete a finished one that was not installed

label: Denoise Model Downloads
params_doc: {} → {running, downloads: [{id, state: running | done | installed | failed | cancelled, bytes, total, error, from}]} — also installs any download that has arrived

params_doc: {path} → model terms from an adjacent manifest; never executes the file

label: Install Denoise Model
params_doc: {path, acknowledged: true, activate?: true, background?: false} → {installed, model} or {started} — install a denoise model from a file: an .onnx with a denoise-model.json beside it, or an archive LightCraft knows (the darktable `.dtmodel`). `acknowledged` must be true: the user has been shown the model's licence and accepted it. Unless `activate` is false it becomes the model in use

label: Denoise Models
params_doc: {} → {dir, productsDir, model, runtime, auto, cacheGb, threads, runOn, models: [{id, name, version, licence{name, commercial, url, notice}, provenance, source, sizeBytes, sha256, tile, known, downloadHost, installed, selected, accepted}]}

label: Remove Denoise Model
params_doc: {id} → {removed, model} — delete an installed model (its cached pictures stay until they are evicted)

params_doc: {id: installed model | null} → {model} — null uses the built-in denoiser

params_doc: {id} → {ok, result} — load an installed model and check it gives sensible pictures; needs the denoise runtime

label: Denoise Pump
params_doc: {pace?: pause | light | normal | full} → {active, running, queued, ready, generation, downloading} — called every frame by the app: takes in finished work and keeps one photo going

params_doc: {ids?: [photoId], scope?: selected | visible | withAmount, retry?: false} → {added, …status} — make the denoised pictures of raw photos that have none, in the background. `retry` tries photos that failed before

label: Denoise Settings
params_doc: {auto?: bool, cacheGb?: 1..10000, threads?: 1..64 | null, runOn?: auto | gpu | cpu} → the settings — `auto`: make the picture of the photos being looked at that have a Denoise amount; `cacheGb`: how much the cached pictures may take; `threads`: most tiles run at once; `runOn`: where the model runs — `auto` (the default) the graphics card where it is faster than the processor (both timed on this computer when the card is set up), `gpu` the card whenever it can run the model, `cpu` the processor. Setting `runOn` also lets the card be tried again after a set-up that failed or closed LightCraft

label: Denoise Status
params_doc: {id?} → {enabled, model, runtime, productsDir, queued, running: {photo, done, total, seconds} | null, ready, made, auto, runOn, device: {kind: gpu | cpu | pending | none, adapter?, reason?, cardMs?, cpuMs?, fellBack?, remote?: {address, state: pending | unavailable | used | idle | slower | given up, device?, remoteMs?, localMs?, reason?, failures?, lastError?}}, cache: {files, bytes, limitBytes}, generation, photo?: {state: notApplicable | ready | queued | running | failed | idle, …}}

label: AI Denoise
params_doc: {id?: photoId, enabled?: bool} → {id, enabled, amount} — turn AI Denoise on (50% initially) or off for one raw photo, independent of selection and Auto Sync; uses the built-in denoiser when no model is chosen

params_doc: {ids?, groups?: [settingsGroup] (paste only these of the copied groups)}

params_doc: {bw?: bool} (toggles when omitted)

params_doc: {ids?}: moves the target photos (`ids`, else the selection) that are on an older rendering process to the current one, as one undo step (their look can change; the sliders keep their values; see docs/process-versions.md). params_doc: {mode: asShot|auto|daylight|cloudy|shade|tungsten|fluorescent|flash|custom, temp?, tint?}

label: White Balance Selector
params_doc: {x, y} normalized image coords of a neutral point

params_doc: {paths: [absolute file paths], album?: name (an album at the top level of Photos, made when missing; default none), wait?} → once Photos is done, {job, running: false, requested, album, imported, ids: [Photos media item ids], warning?}; with wait: false, at once {job, running: true, requested, album} and the outcome later from export.photosImports {job}. wait defaults to true without a window (lightcraft-cli, the MCP server) and to false in the desktop app, where wait: true is refused (its control requests are answered on the UI thread, which never waits for Photos). macOS: asks Photos to import the files (the first time, macOS asks the user to allow LightCraft to control Photos). params_doc: {path, ids?: photo ids (default selection), paper?: a4|letter, landscape?: bool, columns?: 1..8, rows?: 1..10, captions?: bool} → {path, pages, photos, bytes}; replaces an existing output, never an original

params_doc: {name} — removes a user preset → presets

params_doc: {job?} → {imports: [{job, running, exporting?, requested, album, imported?, ids?, warning?, error?, skipped?}]} (this session's, oldest first), or the one job: how Add to Apple Photos is getting on (exporting: reserved by an export still writing its files)

params_doc: {} → [{name, builtin, params}] (use with app.export {preset: name, …overrides})

params_doc: {name, params?: app.export params (default: the last export's)} — adds or replaces a user preset, saved with the library → presets

params_doc: {ids?, apply?: bool (default true), score?: 0.6, nmsIou?: 0.3, maxFaces?} → {photos: [{id, faces: [{rect, score, landmarks}]}]}. Finds faces with the YuNet detector (download it first: `faces.models.download {id: "yunet-2023mar"}`) and, unless `apply` is false, adds them as unnamed face regions (one undo step), replacing earlier detections but never regions from XMP or ones you named; the sidecar is not touched

params_doc: {enabled?: bool} (toggles when omitted)

params_doc: {budgetMs?: 0, burstSecs?: 5, margin?, thresholds?: [..], scope?: "visible"} → {queries, top1, sweep: [{threshold, suggested, correct, precision, recall}]} — leave-one-out over your named faces: each is ranked against the others (ignoring shots within burstSecs of it) to show how well the chosen model recognises people in *your* photos and which threshold to trust. Faces not yet embedded are done within budgetMs (`faces.index` does them all); counts only

params_doc: {cpuOnly?: bool} → {cpuOnly, detection, recognition}: where the face models run, each as {checking, device, why} (null until it is loaded). label: Index Faces
params_doc: {budgetMs?: 200, ids?: [photo ids to do first]} → {embedded, photosDone, pendingPhotos, indexedFaces, ms} — embed the faces in the library with the chosen recognition model, as many photos as fit in the time (at least one); call again until `pendingPhotos` is 0. `budgetMs: 0` only reports

label: Download Face Model
params_doc: {id, acknowledged: true} → {started, from} — fetch a recognition model LightCraft has a pinned address for (see `downloadHost` in the list), in the background over pure-Rust https (lightcraft-fetch). `acknowledged` must be true: the user has been shown the model's terms and accepted them. It is checked against its size and SHA-256, then installed, chosen and switched on by itself; `faces.models.downloads` shows how far it is

params_doc: {id} → {discarded} — stop a download, or delete a finished one that was not installed

params_doc: {path} → what a .onnx file is: {kind: known | draft | unsupported, model, assumptions, reason, alreadyInstalled}; installs nothing

params_doc: {path, acknowledged: true, activate?: true} → {installed, active: {embedder, enabled}} — copy a .onnx face recognition model into the models folder. `acknowledged` must be true: the user has been shown its licence (see inspect) and accepted it. label: Face Models
params_doc: {} → {dir, enabled, embedder, runtime, models: [{id, name, role, licence{name, commercial, url, notice}, provenance, source, sizeBytes, known, installed, selected}]}

params_doc: {id} — delete an installed model

params_doc: {id: installed recogniser | null}

params_doc: {id} → {ok, result: {loadMs, embedMs, dimension, checks}} — load an installed recognition model and check it gives sensible faces; needs the recognition runtime

params_doc: {faces: [{photo, index}], name} → {named, photos} — name (or, with a null or empty name, clear) many face regions as one undoable step; the sidecar is not touched

label: Faces of a Person
params_doc: {name, more?: 120} → {name, total, confirmed: [{photo, index, rect}], more: [{photo, index, rect, score}], ready, pendingPhotos} — the faces named `name` across the library, and the unnamed faces that look most like them (best first, already embedded ones only, once recognition is on); confirm one with `faces.setName`

params_doc: {from, to, merge?: bool} → {faces, photos, from, to, merged} — give every in-library face of `from` the name `to` (trimmed, any capitalization), one undo step; refused when `to` is already someone else unless `merge` is true, which combines the two; the sidecar is not touched

params_doc: {id?, index, name} — name a face region (null or empty clears it); undoable; the sidecar is not touched

label: Suggest Names for Faces
params_doc: {ids?, threshold?, margin?, budgetMs?} → {photos: [{id, faces: [{index, suggestion: {name, score, runnerUp} | null, candidates: [{name, score}]}]}]} — who the unnamed faces in these photos might be, from the faces already named in the library. Only suggestions: nothing is named

label: Unnamed Faces
params_doc: {limit?: 600} → {total, faces: [{photo, index, rect, view, suggestion: {name, score} | null}], ordered, ready} — the faces nobody has named; with recognition running, look-alikes are next to each other and a face the named ones recognise carries the name they suggest. `view` is the box to show the face by. label: Delete Filter Preset
params_doc: {name}

params_doc: {} → [{name, filter}]
